name: Semax

b.x: 226 PubMed citations and a prescription approval in Russia. That track record separates Semax (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, ACTH 4-10 analog) from most peptides in the nootropic category. The mechanism is centered on BDNF. Dolotov and colleagues confirmed that a single Semax dose at 50 mcg/kg produced a 3-fold increase in BDNF mRNA and a 1.4-fold increase in BDNF protein in the rat hippocampus [1]. A separate group showed binding-specific increases in BDNF protein in the basal forebrain [2]. Beyond neurotrophins, Semax activates dopaminergic and serotonergic systems without touching cortisol, unlike its parent molecule ACTH. In practice, the community doses 300 to 600 mcg intranasally each morning for 10 to 14 days. Thousands of user reports across r/Peptides, r/nootropics, and Longecity describe improved focus, verbal fluency, and working memory starting within the first few days. The Selank stack (300 mcg of each, intranasal AM) is the most popular combination, adding anxiolytic balance to the dopaminergic stimulation. Gusev and colleagues followed 110 stroke patients in Russia and found higher plasma BDNF in those given Semax courses. A 2025 study in transgenic Alzheimer's mice showed reduced amyloid plaques [3]. Another 2025 paper in the British Journal of Pharmacology identified a new mu-opioid receptor mechanism for spinal cord injury recovery [4]. The science is expanding, but it still leans heavily on animal models and small Russian clinical samples. No placebo-controlled RCT has been run in healthy adults at any dose.

Semax is a synthetic analog of ACTH(4-10) with a Pro-Gly-Pro C-terminal extension. It binds melanocortin receptors MC3R and MC4R in the brain without activating adrenal cortisol production. That selectivity is what separates it from full-length ACTH. The primary action runs through BDNF upregulation. Dolotov's group showed that 50 mcg/kg of Semax produced a 3-fold increase in exon III BDNF mRNA and a 1.4-fold increase in BDNF protein in the hippocampus [1]. TrkB receptor phosphorylation jumped 1.6-fold in the same study. Grigoriev and colleagues confirmed Semax raised NGF levels in the basal forebrain through a separate pathway [2]. The neurotrophin response begins within hours and accumulates across a 10 to 20 day cycle. The downstream signaling is broad. Semax modulates dopamine and serotonin turnover in the striatum and prefrontal cortex [5]. A genome-wide analysis of Semax in rat focal ischemia identified changes across immune, vascular, and neuroplasticity gene networks [6]. In 2025, a British Journal of Pharmacology paper revealed a previously unknown mu-opioid receptor and FTO deubiquitination mechanism relevant to spinal cord injury recovery [4]. Plasma half-life is only 2 to 3 minutes intravenously. The functional duration, though, runs 20 to 24 hours. That disconnect comes from the BDNF cascade itself; once BDNF and TrkB signaling are triggered, the downstream neuroplasticity changes continue long after the peptide clears the blood.
Semax benefits center on BDNF-driven cognitive performance, neuroprotection, and short-cycle convenience.

Hippocampal BDNF triples with a single dose. Dolotov and colleagues confirmed 3-fold BDNF mRNA increase and 1.4-fold BDNF protein increase at 50 mcg/kg in rats [1]. TrkB receptor phosphorylation increased 1.6-fold in the same study.

Approved for stroke recovery in Russia. Gusev and colleagues followed 110 stroke patients in Russia; those given Semax courses had higher plasma BDNF and better daily-function scores (Zh Nevrol Psikhiatr 2018). The neuroprotective indication is backed by the largest clinical dataset for this peptide.

Cognitive benefits persist 1 to 3 weeks after stopping. That residual effect is consistently cited across thousands of community reports on r/Peptides and Longecity; it is the primary reason users prefer short cycles over continuous dosing.
Focus and working memory improve within days. Community users describe sharper verbal fluency and sustained attention starting by day 2 to 4, peaking around days 8 to 14 of a cycle.
No cortisol disruption. Unlike ACTH, Semax does not stimulate the adrenal glands. You get the neurotrophic benefits without hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis interference.

Human data is limited to small Russian clinical trials in stroke and cognitive disorder patients; no placebo-controlled RCTs in healthy adults exist. 2025 studies extend preclinical evidence to Alzheimer's transgenic models and spinal cord injury via a newly identified μ-opioid receptor pathway.
Key Study

Dolotov et al. 2006 (PMID 16996037): Semax regulates BDNF and TrkB in rat hippocampus; Gusev et al. 2018 (PMID 29798983): 110 stroke patients, Semax vs. no-Semax subgroups (not placebo-controlled), higher plasma BDNF and Barthel scores; PMID 41479572 (2025): Semax reduced amyloid plaques in transgenic AD mice; PMID 40692165 (2025, British J Pharmacology): μ-opioid receptor / FTO deubiquitination mechanism for SCI recovery
Limitations

Majority of evidence from rodent and cell models. Human trials conducted in Russia (stroke, cognitive disorders) with limited published methodological detail. No placebo-controlled RCTs in healthy adults at any dose. Mechanism of prolonged functional duration (20-24h BDNF cascade from 2-3 min plasma t½) is documented but not fully characterized at human doses.

Reconstitution math for the standard setup: 5 mg vial plus 2 mL bacteriostatic water gives you 2500 mcg/mL. On a U-100 insulin syringe, 200 mcg is 8 IU, 300 mcg is 12 IU, 400 mcg is 16 IU, 500 mcg is 20 IU. For pre-made nasal spray (common at 30 mg/10 mL = 3000 mcg/mL), verify the mcg-per-spray on the label before dosing. Spray calibration varies between atomizers. Morning only. Nothing after noon. The dopaminergic tail will disrupt your sleep if you dose late. This is the single most common correctable complaint in community reports. Start at 200 mcg. Assess tolerance for 3 days before moving to 300 mcg. The response curve is clear in the community data; 300 to 500 mcg is where most users settle. If you feel nothing by day 5, check three things. Is the vial refrigerated and under 21 days post-reconstitution? Is the reconstitution volume correct (a dilution error is the most common source problem)? Did you actually dose in the morning on an empty stomach? Advancing to 400 mcg is reasonable after ruling those out. Stacking with Selank 300 mcg intranasal takes the edge off for users sensitive to the dopaminergic stimulation. That combination is the community default for good reason.

Reconstitute the vial Add 2 mL of bacteriostatic water to a 5 mg Semax vial. This gives you 2500 mcg/mL. Swirl gently, do not shake. Let the powder dissolve fully before drawing.

Draw your dose For subcutaneous injection, use a 29 to 31 gauge insulin syringe (U-100). 200 mcg equals 8 IU. 300 mcg equals 12 IU. 500 mcg equals 20 IU. For intranasal, transfer the reconstituted solution to a calibrated nasal atomizer or use a pre-made spray.

Subcutaneous route: clean the injection site (abdomen or thigh) with an alcohol swab. Pinch the skin and insert the needle at a 45-degree angle. Inject slowly and withdraw. Rotate injection sites between doses. Onset is approximately 30 minutes.

Intranasal route: clear your nasal passages with saline Tilt your head slightly forward. Insert the spray tip into one nostril, close the other, press once and inhale gently. For doses above 200 mcg, split across both nostrils with a 5-minute pause between sides. Onset is approximately 15 minutes.
Time it right Dose in the morning, before 10 AM. Do not dose after noon. The dopaminergic alerting effect lasts 20 to 24 hours at the functional level.
Store properly Refrigerate the reconstituted vial at 2 to 8 degrees C. Use within 21 days. Keep unreconstituted lyophilized powder refrigerated for long-term storage.

Sleep disruption is the most consistently reported problem, and it is almost always a timing error. Semax increases dopamine turnover. Dosing after noon delays sleep onset for hours. Restricting administration to before 10 AM resolves the issue for most users. Even a 2 PM dose can wreck that night's sleep architecture. Anxiety and irritability rank second. The effect is dose-dependent. At 600 mcg per day and above, community reports of agitation, frustration with interruptions, and generalized anxiety increase sharply. Users with pre-existing anxiety disorders face the highest risk. Reducing the dose by 50% typically resolves the issue within 1 to 2 days. Stacking with Selank 300 mcg mitigates anxiety for most users; that combination is the most popular community protocol for exactly this reason. Nasal irritation affects intranasal users during the first week. Mild burning, tingling, and dryness at the mucosal surface are common and generally self-limiting. A saline rinse between doses helps. For persistent irritation, switching to subcutaneous injection eliminates the local effect entirely. Afternoon fatigue and a "comedown" feeling appear at doses of 600 mcg per day and higher. Splitting the dose into 2 administrations (morning and before 1 PM) or reducing to 300 to 400 mcg often solves this. Emotional blunting or mental flatness is reported with sustained use above 600 mcg per day beyond day 14. A minority of users running extended high-dose cycles also report reduced libido. Both effects resolve after stopping. Hair thinning has been described at very high doses over long periods. The reports are rare and uniformly described as reversible. Melanocortin receptor (MC4R) activation is the speculated mechanism. Human safety data is limited. The published literature comes from Russian clinical trials in stroke and cognitive disorder patients, not healthy adult nootropic users. No formal adverse event reporting exists for the community dosing context. Contraindications: pregnancy or breastfeeding (no safety data), known hypersensitivity to ACTH-derived peptides, active intracranial hypertension, history of seizure disorders (limited data, use with caution), and children under 18 without physician supervision. SSRIs and SNRIs require monitoring because Semax modulates serotonin systems; additive serotonergic effects are possible. Dopaminergic drugs (L-DOPA, dopamine agonists) carry additive stimulation risk; dose adjustment may be needed. Stop use and consult a physician if anxiety persists despite morning-only dosing at 300 mcg or below, if sleep disruption does not resolve with timing changes, or if blood pressure exceeds 130/80 mmHg.
Common Issues & Solutions
Sleep disruption: Semax has a dopaminergic alerting effect. Restrict dosing strictly to before 10am. Even a 2pm dose can delay sleep onset: timing is the most common correctable cause.
Post-dose afternoon fatigue: Reported at doses ≥600 mcg/day. Reduce to 300–400 mcg or split into two smaller doses (AM + early afternoon, not after 1pm) rather than a single large dose.
Nasal irritation: Burning or dryness with intranasal use typically resolves within the first week. Rinse with sterile saline between doses. For persistent irritation, switch to subQ injection.
Anxiety / irritability: Usually dose-dependent. Reduce dose by 50% and reassess. Stacking with Selank 300 mcg mitigates anxiety for most users. If anxiety persists at ≤300 mcg/day, discontinue.

No perceived effects: Verify vial was stored refrigerated post-reconstitution and used within 21 days. Confirm morning-only dosing. Advance from 200 mcg to 400 mcg if no effect by day 5. Also confirm reconstitution volume is correct: under-concentrated vials are a common source issue.

Semax holds marketing authorization in Russia and Ukraine as a prescription drug for stroke recovery, cognitive disorders, and peptic ulcers. It has no FDA approval and no active IND application in any Western jurisdiction. Semax was on the FDA Category 2 bulk drug substance list until its nominators withdrew it; FDA's Category 2 page (current as of April 22, 2026) lists it as withdrawn. PCAC discussed Semax on July 24, 2026. No FDA rule has added it to the 503A bulks list, so compounding pharmacies cannot use it today. In the US it is sold online as a research chemical labeled for in-vitro research use. WADA status is uncertain. Semax is an ACTH analog with melanocortin receptor activity. Athletes subject to drug testing should treat it as a risk and consult their sport's anti-doping authority. This content is for informational and educational purposes only. It does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any research compound.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Semax dosage?
faqs.a: Beginner: 200 mcg intranasal, 1-2 times daily. Moderate: 500 mcg intranasal or subcutaneous daily. Aggressive: 1,000 mcg daily. Approved Russian protocols use 200-600 mcg/day intranasal for 10-14 day cycles. N-Acetyl Semax Amidate (NASA) is the most popular modified form in Western communities.

Semax is a synthetic ACTH(4-10) analog, meaning it's a modified fragment of the adrenocorticotropic hormone. It increases BDNF and NGF expression, which supports neuroplasticity and nerve growth. The mechanism does not involve cortisol elevation despite the ACTH origin. Russian clinical data across 226 PubMed-indexed papers supports cognitive and neuroprotective applications.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of Semax?
faqs.a: Semax has a favorable side effect profile in Russian clinical use. Reported effects include mild nasal irritation (intranasal route), occasional headache, and rare dizziness. No dependency, withdrawal, or significant adverse events have been documented in published studies. The short plasma half-life (2-3 minutes IV) limits systemic exposure.

faqs.q: How long should you cycle Semax?
faqs.a: Standard cycles run 10-20 days on, followed by an equal off period. This mirrors the structure of approved Russian clinical protocols. Community users report diminishing cognitive benefits after approximately day 12-14 of continuous use, consistent with melanocortin receptor adaptation and BDNF pathway normalization.

Semax is not FDA-approved in the United States but holds prescription approval in Russia for stroke recovery and cognitive enhancement. It was approved by the Russian Ministry of Health in 2011. US availability is limited to research-grade products and select compounding arrangements.

faqs.a: The half-life of Semax is ~2-3 min (IV). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: . Semax (ACTH 4-10 analog, Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic heptapeptide approved in Russia for stroke recovery and cognitive disorders since the 1990s. No placebo-controlled randomized trials exist in healthy adults. The cognitive effects last 1 to 3 weeks after you stop dosing, which is the rationale behind short 10 to 20 day cycles. Users chasing sharper focus, better working memory, and sustained neuroplasticity without long-term daily commitment tend to reach for this one over racetams and stimulants.
